newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia noon rubber stays under baht pressure.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia noon rubber stays under baht pressure.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were down slightly at noon as the market remained under pressure from the steep fall in Thai rubber values due to the baht flotation.
"If we don't follow them, our goods can't catch up with their price," a rubber trader in Kuala Lumpur said, explaining the huge price corrections seen in the local market since late Wednesday.

At midday, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted August buyers of the benchmark RSS1 at 248 Malaysian cents (98 U.S. cents) a kg, down 1.50 cents from Wednesday's close. August SMR20 buyer was a cent down to 241.
Local dealers said that despite adjustments, the SMR20 was still at a premium of six to seven cents against the Thai TSR20.
"We've heard that the Thai boys are selling heavily in U.S. dollars to protect themselves against any real effect of the currency devaluation," said another trader.
"Our prices must come down a little more if we are to compete evenly with them," he added.
At noon, trading houses offered the SMR20 at 238 cents, SMR10 at 239, SMR5 at 252, SMR CV at 309, SMR L at 290 and drum latex at 205.
